The NHD-600-E encoder and decoder delivers cost-optimized, high-performance SDVoE AV over IP transmission and reception. The “E” variations remove some of the I/O found on the standard encoder and decoder and retain only the core functionalities that suite most applications. Engineered for installations requiring pixel-perfect 4K60 4:4:4 video with zero-frame latency, this series supports robust 10GbE network operation with PoE+ power and a flexible AV control suite.

Deliver pixel-perfect, lossless video with support for up to 4K60 4:4:4 over HDMI 2.0, including HDR formats such as HDR10, HLG, and Dolby Vision (low latency). The SDVoE architecture ensures uncompromised image quality and zero-frame latency, while analog audio support enables flexible audio routing or de-embedding alongside HDMI audio.

Designed for streamlined installation, the NHD-600-E supports PoE+ (802.3at) power to reduce cabling complexity. HDMI 2.0 connectivity is provided on both encoder and decoder models, alongside analog audio connections and bidirectional IR and RS-232 passthrough for seamless integration with external devices.

Built on a 10GbE SDVoE network backbone, the 600-E enables reliable AV distribution across point-to-point and matrix-based systems. Integrated support for network-based control allows IR and RS-232 signals to be transmitted alongside video and audio, ensuring compatibility with third-party control platforms and automation systems.

Powered by SDVoE technology, the NHD-600-E delivers true zero-frame latency for real-time video transmission. This ensures perfectly synchronized audio and video, making it ideal for live presentation environments, control rooms, and interactive AV systems where timing accuracy is critical.

Is there a dedicated AV network or will one be provided?
positioningNotes: Use for architectural judgement, product-family selection and proposal-safe trade-off language.
Be explicit when the product is technically possible but unlikely to be the most natural choice.
Use for flexible and expandable systems, not simply because there are multiple screens.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not let a feature match override the real application, architecture or operational requirement.
Do not use AV-over-IP to overcomplicate a small fixed room when a matrix or HDBaseT solution fits better.
